batch_patterns.evidence: keys DDDDBBADABCADACCBCBCDBCDABDCCDCABBDBBCCC: A 6/40 vs B 11, C 12, D 11 (A under-used); runs of D on items 1-4 (all four detail/inference keys of the canning lecture) and C on items 38-40. Mild; not enough alone to pick keys but A is the safest letter to eliminate.

in each, exactly two options share a stem and differ in one element, and the key is always one of the twin pair (9: "whether the woman should keep hens, which ..." x2; 14: "Twenty, ..." x2; 26: "It would end up smaller/larger ..."; 30: "Two ideas for the old depot ..." x2) - 4/4, reduces each item to a coin flip without the audio.

both conversation gist items key the UNDECIDED / deferred outcome ("which they will decide later"; "that the club will vote on") against a twin distractor asserting a decision ("which the man agrees to at last"; "and choosing the letter"); a student who learns that pattern answers both without listening.
